expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: Opens with: "No, a 'table isn't empty' check wouldn't have caught this incident."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "The COALESCE to zero" section: "It converts 'I don't know' into 'zero' — and in revenue context, those are catastrophically different."

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconciliation to source": "Daily: does SUM(revenue) in your table match SUM(revenue) in the source system?"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: Discusses prevention via contracts and detection via reconciliation, but does not explicitly recommend assertions block or run before dashboard publication

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Data contract on the source (Control)" with example: "columns: - name: revenue_amount # exact name, not 'whatever's there'"

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Volume vs. historical baseline": "Is today's revenue within 2 standard deviations..." and "Null rate monitoring on join columns"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Mentions "Three weeks of decisions were made with wrong data" but does not frame the 3-week detection delay as its own hazard requiring instrumentation

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: "silence is the defect. The pipeline succeeded. The numbers looked plausible. The COALESCE to zero actively hid the problem"; shows how wrong data gets acted upon
